title: "Overview"

Python parity layer over the IMF/World Bank **LIC-DSF** Excel template.
If you already know the workbook (Inputs, Ext/Dom/Macro, Baseline, stresses, CI,
Outputs), these pages map sheets to packages and point at runnable demos.

## 10-minute path

1. Install (from a checkout): `uv sync --all-groups`
2. Open [`getting-started.qmd`](getting-started.qmd) or run
   [`demo/all_outputs.ipynb`](https://github.com/Teal-Insights/py-lic-dsf/blob/main/demo/all_outputs.ipynb)
3. Bookmark [`excel-map.qmd`](excel-map.qmd) for sheet → code lookup

Bundled template: [`data/lic-dsf-template-2025-08-12.xlsx`](https://github.com/Teal-Insights/py-lic-dsf/blob/main/data/lic-dsf-template-2025-08-12.xlsx)
(see [`NOTICE.md`](https://github.com/Teal-Insights/py-lic-dsf/blob/main/NOTICE.md) for IMF/World Bank provenance).

## Python mental model

| Idea | Role |
|------|------|
| **Loader** | Reads Input / sheet blocks from a `.xlsx` into typed inputs |
| **Book** | Sheet engine (`ExternalDebtBook`, `MacroDebtBook`, baseline/stress books) |
| **Panel** | Output-shaped `pandas.DataFrame` (rows ≈ Excel indicators, columns = years) |
| **Portfolio** | New MLT instruments behind Ext (`PVPortfolio`) |

Typical flow: load workbook → build Ext + Macro books → baseline / stress panels →
rating.

MIT covers the Python source. The bundled LIC-DSF template remains an IMF/World
Bank work — see [`NOTICE.md`](https://github.com/Teal-Insights/py-lic-dsf/blob/main/NOTICE.md) and [`data/PROVENANCE.md`](https://github.com/Teal-Insights/py-lic-dsf/blob/main/data/PROVENANCE.md).

## Output-panel parity (live Excel)

Default `uv run pytest` stays Excel-free (`-m 'not live_excel'`). Coverage is
the **probe catalog** for Output sheets (row-keyed 1-1/1-2, scenario-keyed
3-x, cell-keyed 5/7) — not every formula on Ext/Macro/B.

The system under test is the Excel-shaped table (`output_11_table`,
`output_31_table`, …). The oracle is **live Microsoft Excel** (xlwings/COM)
on the official `.xlsm`:

```bash
uv sync --extra excel
LIC_DSF_EXCEL=1 uv run pytest -m live_excel   # Windows + Excel
```

Linux CI never starts Excel. Cached `data_only` cells in the bundled `.xlsx`
are a convenience for unit tests, not the official oracle.

Inventory of numeric Output rows: [`data/parity/output_inventory.csv`](https://github.com/Teal-Insights/py-lic-dsf/blob/main/data/parity/output_inventory.csv)
(regenerate with `uv run python -m tests.parity.inventory`).
Side-by-side CSV builders: `tests.parity.compare_probes` and the existing
`compare_realism1` / `compare_outputs_5_7` helpers.
